assets.prompt:
Use case: ads-marketing.
Create a finished, flat digital brand graphic, not a screenshot of a webpage or a physical mockup. Match the current portfolio's visual language: warm white #f8f8f6, nearly black #20221f, secondary warm gray #5b5e58, very restrained terracotta #b2472c. Bold Inter-like editorial sans serif with tight but readable spacing; small monospaced role captions. Crisp text, generous whitespace, simple left alignment. Use the exact existing D/I monogram from the logo reference: white D slash I with straight horizontal I terminals on a nearly black square, subtly rounded corners. Do not redesign the mark.
The website reference supplies style only: do not reproduce its portrait, navigation, action buttons or availability details unless explicitly requested below.
Avoid blue, gradients, noise, decorative background grids, outer frames, vertical divider lines, pill shapes, fake metrics, watermarks and decorative icons. Never add unrequested text. All requested copy must be rendered verbatim in correct English and legible at LinkedIn thumbnail size.
Asset type: LinkedIn personal profile cover, a very wide 4:1 banner, final canvas 3168 x 792 pixels.
Inputs: image 1 is the old cover to replace, used ONLY for its very wide aspect ratio and placement purpose. Image 2 is the current website and primary style reference. Image 3 is the exact logo reference.
Replace the old cover with a calm, confident typographic composition. Leave the LEFTMOST 25% of the banner almost empty, especially its lower half: LinkedIn's separate profile avatar overlaps this area. Do not include a portrait or avatar.
Put a small D/I logo and “Danila Igoshin” at the top-left in the safe upper area. The main content starts around 28% of canvas width. Above the headline, set this small but readable role line:
“PRODUCT ENGINEER / FULL-STACK ENGINEER”
Large headline on exactly three lines:
“B2B products.”
“From zero to”
“production.”
Make all headline letters dark, not terracotta. Before the third line, place one short, thin terracotta horizontal dash and indent “production.” as in the new website. The headline occupies roughly 43% of banner width, with clear margins above and below.
At the far right, a compact calm text block:
“Frontend first.”
“Full-stack when the product needs it.”
Below it:
“danilaigoshin.com”
Keep this supporting text readable and subordinate. Use only these texts, no metrics or thin miniature tables. Preserve the full 4:1 format, with all typography comfortably inside the canvas. This is one upload-ready banner, not a presentation showing a banner inside a border.
